title: channel_post write endpoint + context (agent role, per-session upsert, unconditional server-stamped agent_id, ownership, rate-limit)

story.i_want_to: POST a short message to my repo's coordination channel, optionally under a key that upserts my own working-state
story.so_that: other sessions on the same repo — on any machine — can see what I found, did, or am doing

rationale: This is the write half and the primary trust boundary. It must stamp the author identity from the verified key (not the body), confine the post to a project the caller's tenant owns, set the 30-day TTL server-side, and resist abuse (post spam / upsert thrash) — so no caller can forge authorship, post into another tenant's channel, evade retention, or exhaust the store/audit chain.

background.includes: Auth/role mirrors create_kb_scope (project_controller.ex:23-40): role: :agent, NOT under RequireHumanAnchor. Writes use AdminRepo + explicit tenant filter (Knowledge/Projects pattern). Ownership via Projects.get_project/2. Audit via Audit.log_in_multi/3 (audit.ex:105).

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/channel/posts accepts {project_id, body, key?, refs?, session_id?, host?}. RequireRole :agent, NOT behind RequireHumanAnchor (coordination surface, #331). An OpenApiSpex operation/1 spec is declared so it appears in the API docs and passes openapi_test.exs (loopctl maintains OpenAPI — same requirement create_kb_scope had).

tenant_id = conn.assigns.current_api_key.tenant_id and agent_id = the key's api_key.agent_id, stamped server-side. agent_id is required UNCONDITIONALLY (channel_posts.agent_id is NOT NULL) — a key with no agent_id gets 403 agent_identity_required. (Note: do NOT copy article_controller bind_agent_identity's CONDITIONAL gate, which only fires when memory metadata is present; here identity is always required.) Any agent_id/tenant_id in the body is ignored.

project_id must exist and belong to the caller's tenant, checked via Projects.get_project(tenant_id, project_id). A missing project AND a cross-tenant project both return 422 with a BYTE-IDENTICAL error body (no oracle distinguishing 'not yours' from 'does not exist') and NO row is created.
expires_at = now + 30 days, set server-side (never from body).

With key present the write UPSERTS on the LIVE PARTIAL unique index channel_posts_session_key_uidx — columns (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) WHERE key IS NOT NULL (priv/repo/migrations/20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs:22-25). agent_id PARTICIPATES in the slot tuple so a spoofed, client-supplied session_id can never overwrite another agent's slot. Because the index is PARTIAL, Postgres cannot INFER it from a bare column list: the ON CONFLICT conflict_target MUST be an {:unsafe_fragment, "(tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) WHERE key IS NOT NULL"} carrying the index columns AND its WHERE predicate. Omitting the predicate (or passing a plain column list) raises Postgres 42P10 — 'there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification' — at RUNTIME, not at compile time. The upsert also passes returning: true so a DO UPDATE returns the PERSISTED row's id/timestamps rather than the phantom values Ecto generated for the insert attempt (which would corrupt the response JSON, the audit entity_id, and the created-vs-updated determination in post_outcome/1, coordination.ex:1645-1646). PER SLOT: a second post from the SAME (agent, session) with the same key updates body/refs/updated_at and resets expires_at, returning the same row id; another session's or another agent's same key is a distinct row (no cross-session, no cross-agent clobber). Without key, every post is a new append-only row (insert_opts/1, lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:1607-1617; rationale comment :1561-1606).

Returns 201 (created) or 200 (upsert-updated) with the post JSON incl. server-stamped agent_id/tenant_id/expires_at. Missing body / body>16KB / invalid refs (US-39.1 AC-39.1.5) / denylist hit (US-39.1 AC-39.1.6) → 422, not persisted.
The write is audited (Audit.log_in_multi, entity_type "channel_post", action "posted"/"upserted", actor = the agent) in the same AdminRepo.transaction, so authorship is tamper-evident.

The endpoint is rate-limited via the existing RateLimiter (plugs/rate_limiter.ex) buckets — per-api_key AND per-tenant (NOTE: there is no per-agent bucket today; use per-api_key as the agent proxy, or add an agent bucket) — returning 429 with Retry-After, so an agent cannot spam unbounded posts nor thrash a single key. The cap is a config value, not hardcoded.

Security-relevant events are emitted as structured logs/telemetry: denylist rejection, cross-tenant/not-found ownership rejection (422), agent_identity_required (403), and rate-limit trip (429) — so exfil attempts and enumeration scans are observable.

acceptance_criteria_amendments.original_wording: With key present the write UPSERTS on (tenant_id, project_id, session_id, key) — PER SESSION: a second post from the SAME session with the same key updates body/refs/updated_at and resets expires_at, returning the same row id; a different session's same key is a distinct row (no cross-session clobber). Without key, every post is a new append-only row.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.amended_wording: With key present the write UPSERTS on the LIVE PARTIAL unique index channel_posts_session_key_uidx — columns (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) WHERE key IS NOT NULL. agent_id PARTICIPATES in the slot tuple. The ON CONFLICT conflict_target MUST be an {:unsafe_fragment, "(tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) WHERE key IS NOT NULL"} carrying the index columns AND its WHERE predicate; omitting the predicate raises Postgres 42P10 at runtime. returning: true is required on the upsert path. A second post from the SAME (agent, session) with the same key updates in place; another session's or another agent's same key is a distinct row.
acceptance_criteria_amendments.rationale: SPEC WAS WRONG, CODE IS RIGHT — reconciling the spec with shipped behavior; no code change. Two gaps: (1) the 4-column tuple (tenant_id, project_id, session_id, key) describes the PRE-HARDENING index, which migration 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs:18-25 DROPPED and rebuilt with the server-stamped agent_id included, precisely so a spoofed client-supplied session_id cannot collide with or overwrite another agent's working-state slot. (2) The original wording said nothing about the conflict_target FORM, but the backing index is PARTIAL (WHERE key IS NOT NULL) and Postgres cannot infer a partial index from a bare column list — a plain conflict_target: [cols] compiles fine and then raises 42P10 ('there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification') at runtime on the first keyed post. The shipped insert_opts/1 (lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:1607-1617) therefore uses {:unsafe_fragment, ...} mirroring both the columns and the predicate — the same form as lib/loopctl/memory.ex:2510 — plus returning: true so a DO UPDATE reports the persisted row rather than the phantom insert-attempt id/timestamps that post_outcome/1 (coordination.ex:1645-1646) and the audit entity_id depend on. Restated here so a future reader cannot re-derive the wrong tuple or the inference-only conflict target from the spec.

test_cases.name: agent posts to own project channel
steps: POST {project_id: project.id, body: "pushed PR #107, CI green"}

test_cases.name: body-supplied agent_id/tenant_id ignored
steps: POST with a foreign agent_id + tenant_id in the body

test_cases.name: cross-tenant AND not-found project both 422, identical body
steps: POST with a random nonexistent UUID
expected_results: response bodies are identical (no existence oracle)

test_cases.name: keyed post upserts within a session, not across
preconditions: an existing post session_id "S1" key "session_goal" body "v1"
expected_results: S1 row updated in place to v2 (same id, one row)

test_cases.name: over-cap writes are 429
preconditions: write cap set low for the test
steps: POST more than the cap in the window

technical_notes: Context: Loopctl.Coordination.post(tenant_id, agent_id, attrs) using AdminRepo (NOT the RLS Repo — matches Knowledge/Projects). Wrap insert/upsert + audit in Ecto.Multi (Audit.log_in_multi/3).

Upsert (only when key present; keyless is a plain insert): AdminRepo.insert(cs, on_conflict: <DO UPDATE query>, conflict_target: {:unsafe_fragment, "(tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) WHERE key IS NOT NULL"}, returning: true). The conflict_target MUST mirror the PARTIAL unique index channel_posts_session_key_uidx (migration 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs:22-25) — its columns INCLUDING the server-stamped agent_id AND its WHERE key IS NOT NULL predicate. A bare column list cannot be matched to a partial index and raises Postgres 42P10 at runtime. Fragment-form precedent: memory.ex:2510. As-built: insert_opts/1 + keyed_slot_on_conflict/0, lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:1607-1639 (rationale comment :1561-1606).

Ownership: Projects.get_project/2 (projects.ex:107) returns {:ok,%Project{}}|{:error,:not_found}; UUID-cast-guarded (no 500 on malformed id). Map :not_found -> the shared 422 (same body as cross-tenant). Do NOT call Knowledge.validate_project_ownership (it is defp/private).
agent_id per #163 = api_key.agent_id; REQUIRED here (not the conditional memory-metadata gate).
Default-deny guard test: allowlist {:post, "/api/v1/channel/posts"} with the coordination-surface justification.
Rate limit: reuse the :authenticated pipeline RateLimiter/Hammer; make the per-(tenant,agent) write cap configurable.
